Subject: Erasure verification: hashlist & snapshot attestation

Hi Vanessa,

As part of the upcoming SOC 2 / ISO verification for ClearHarbor we need to validate tenant-level erasure workflows and associated proof artifacts. For the initial checklist, can you please provide the following:  

- A signed manifest (SHA256) listing objects exported for a sample of 10 tenants (tenant IDs to be provided by us)
- Corresponding export snapshots (metadata + object references) and the S3 locations where these were staged
- Chain of custody documentation for the export process (who initiated, timestamps, access grants)
- The sampling plan you intend to use (how tenants are chosen, sample size justification)

Acceptance criteria: signed manifest using KMS-backed key (or equivalent), linkable snapshots with immutable timestamps, and a simple mapping showing deletion actions taken after export. We would like to receive a draft by close of business Friday, Aug 7th.

Attachments: artifact_request_template.csv (schema)

Thanks,
Marcus Lee
Audit Lead, AuditCorp
AuditCorp - External Audit Services

Subject: Re: Erasure verification: hashlist & snapshot attestation

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the checklist — we can comply. Proposed plan (high level):

1) We will produce a signed SHA256 manifest for a stratified sample of 10 tenants (mix of eu/us/asia where possible).
2) Snapshots (metadata + object refs) will be exported to a time-stamped S3 staging bucket and a zipped bundle will be uploaded to an internal shared drive link.
3) Chain of custody will be a short PDF log showing request -> export -> verification -> deletion, with actor emails and timestamps.
4) KMS key will sign the manifest and we will include the key ID and signature verification instructions.

Target: preliminary artifact bundle by 2026-08-08 EOD; final deliverable by 2026-08-10 after internal spot checks.

Looping in Soojin (Security) and Karthik (Product infra) to confirm timelines and the exact export commands/permissions required.

Attachments: proposed_deliverables_manifest.csv

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa / Marcus,

Quick clarifications from Security:  

- Our export window supports creation of a point-in-time snapshot including object metadata and tenant-mapped keys. Snapshots include creation timestamps and are write-once in the staging bucket (we will enable object lock for the exported prefix).
- Retention TTL for exported staging is 30 days by default; for audit evidence we can request a 90-day hold on the specific audit prefix.
- We will provide instructions for signature verification and the public key material needed to validate the KMS signature.

Operational items for your acceptance criteria:  
- Provide the list of tenant IDs for sampling by Thursday 2026-08-06 12:00pm PT.
- Confirm whether you require full object payloads or metadata+object references only (for PII reasons we recommend metadata+references unless you require payloads).

Attachments: snapshot_export_instructions.md; access_grants_example.csv

Soojin Lee
Head of Security Engineering

Folks,

Technical plan for generating the signed manifest and export snapshots:  

Steps:  
- Trigger export job via infra pipeline (Jira SUP-8127) which will export tenant metadata to s3://redwood-audit-staging/clearharbor/20260805-TIMESTAMP/
- Produce a manifest file listing object keys + lastModified + size + tenant_id. The manifest will be canonicalized (sorted by object key) and hashed using SHA256.
- Use our audit KMS key (projects/redwood/kms/audit-key) to produce an RFC7515-style detached signature of the manifest. We will include key ID and signature metadata.
- Upload signed manifest and sample_hashlist.txt to the staging prefix and copy zipped snapshots to the shared drive link Vanessa mentioned.

Security notes: the export job runs under a temporary service account that has limited IAM and logs to the access ledger. We will include the ledger slice for the export window in the chain_of_custody.pdf.

Timeline: job run on 2026-08-07 morning, preliminary artifact package by 2026-08-08 EOD.

Attachments: sample_hashlist.txt

Karthik Iyer
VP, Product Infrastructure
